card.title: M.S.406
card.flavorText: The M.S.406 was a French fighter aircraft developed by Morane-Saulnier in 1938. At the start of WWII over 1,000 M.S.406s were in French service, which made it France’s most numerous fighter and one of two French fighters capable of 400 km/h. During the Battle for France the aircraft provided mixed results. The aircraft was highly maneuverable, but there were technical setbacks and it had very low firepower. In some cases the M.S.406 was effective, even against the German BF 109, but overall the losses were high (approx. 150 aircraft were lost in combat), and the aircraft is considered to be the least effective French fighter in service during the Battle of France. Many M.S.406s were captured by the Germans after the fall of France, some were used for training purposes while others were sold.
